cultural.vision_reason: A child's white cotton dress with dense cross-stitch embroidery and the characteristic long A-shaped front pocket (pado pandohl) matches classic Baluchi dress construction and decoration.

physical.title: dress
physical.summary: Baluchi-style small child's dress (dishdasha or pashk) made of white cotton with a printed pink pattern. The dress gathers at either side of the waist and, like other Baluchi-style dresses, is characterised by a long A-shaped pocket (pado pandohl) stitched on the front of the skirt to the top of the hem. The pocket is open along one of the short edges. The dress is hand-embroidered with colourful cross-stitched bands on the front and back, including the long pocket, shoulders and sleeve cuffs. The remants of the embroidery patterns that were first inked onto the fabric using wood-block stamps as a guide for the embroiderer are evident around the front of the dress. Can be worn with or without matching baggy trousers (sirwal).
